title: Why Your Edge Model Fails After Deployment
coverHeadline:
Why Your
[[Edge Model]]
Fails in
Production
story: a 98% model misses half the defects on a real factory camera; following the frames from lab to line shows why, and the fix is in the data

scenes.name: Hook
scenes.spoken: Your ninety-eight percent model missed half the defects.
scenes.visual: Frame 0: a lime accuracy chart already at 98% snaps red and drops, with missed-defect markers popping on a camera frame.

scenes.name: Setup
scenes.spoken: In the lab it looked perfect, so you shipped it to the factory camera, and a week later the defect reports started piling up again.
scenes.visual: The hero camera frame travels from a laptop tile to the factory camera tile; a stack of defect reports grows beside it.
cues: In the lab it looked perfect,
so you shipped it to the factory camera,
and a week later the defect reports

scenes.name: Discovery
scenes.onscreen: The lab never saw the glare
scenes.spoken: The lab photos were clean and evenly lit, but the factory has glare from the windows, dust on the lens, and a camera that shakes a little every time the belt moves.
scenes.visual: Same camera frame: glare, dust, and shake effects land on it one by one as each is named.
cues: The lab photos were clean and evenly lit,
but the factory has glare from the windows,
dust on the lens, and a camera

scenes.name: Payoff and takeaway
scenes.onscreen: Test the slice, not the average
scenes.spoken: So before you swap architectures, collect a few hundred frames from that real camera and test on those first, because that's where your accuracy actually lives. Follow for more.
scenes.visual: Frames stream from the camera into a test set card; a per-slice meter for the glare slice climbs. Avatar end card.
